shared_rule: Count an explicitly expressed property/role when its type is established, including an interrogative asking for its value. Do not require the answer value to occur in the input. Never infer a role solely because the task usually needs that parameter; generic domain words alone are not all of its properties.

definitions.general_frequency: An explicitly expressed recurrence, repetition schedule or occurrence-rate role, including a question asking for its rate. The answer value need not be supplied. Apply request-relevant scope.
definitions.time: An explicitly expressed clock time, duration, temporal offset or temporal ordering, including a question asking for a clock reading, duration or offset. The answer value need not be supplied. Preserve separate calendar, day-part and recurrence boundaries and apply request-relevant scope.
definitions.transport_descriptor: An explicitly expressed journey, ticket or transport-service property or qualifier, including a question asking for such a property. Mode, provider identity or location alone is insufficient. Apply request-relevant scope.
definitions.weather_descriptor: An explicitly expressed meteorological condition, property or supported weather-protection criterion, including a question asking for a particular weather property. A generic weather request alone is insufficient. Apply request-relevant scope.

general_frequency: Count an expressed recurrence, repetition schedule or occurrence-rate role, including how often/how frequently questions. A single repeat instruction can refer to repeating one response and does not alone express a recurrence schedule.

Distinguish occurrence rate from elapsed duration, clock time and a one-off calendar anchor. How often is frequency, not automatically time; every three hours explicitly supplies recurrence and a duration interval, so both may hold.
time: Count explicitly expressed clock time, duration, temporal offset or temporal ordering, and questions explicitly asking for a clock time, elapsed duration or offset, even when no answer value is supplied.
What time and temporally interpreted how long establish the role. How long is a river/wall is spatial length, not duration. A time-zone-only question does not by itself ask for a clock reading.

A bare alarm/reminder or an arrival/departure verb does not alone establish this type. How often asks for recurrence, not a clock time or duration. Bare when is unavailable for this predicate if date versus clock/duration scope is unresolved.

Keep calendar periods, day parts and recurrence under their existing type boundaries; do not turn every date, now modifier or tense into time. A requested time property is distinct from the value or executable schedule that answers it.
transport_descriptor: Count an expressed journey/ticket/service property: fare/cost, departure/arrival or service timing/frequency, journey duration, routing qualification, return/round-trip status, accommodation or seat condition. A requested property name counts even without its value.

Transport mode, provider identity, a place or a generic booking/travel request alone is insufficient. A route relation such as via or explicit origin-to-destination routing can qualify a journey; mere location identity cannot.

Assess overlapping time/frequency/place predicates separately. Departure/arrival property evidence does not by itself imply a clock time; how often trains depart supplies frequency and a service property.
weather_descriptor: Count an expressed meteorological condition/property or an explicitly supported weather-protection criterion, including a question asking for temperature, humidity, rainfall or another identified weather property without its answer value.

Generic weather/forecast/climate words alone do not specify a condition/property. Temperature in a cooking, body or device context is not automatically meteorological; ambiguous domain evidence remains unavailable.

A practical clothing/equipment question counts when the utterance establishes a weather-related need, for example rain protection or warmth outside. Sandals, pants, hats, jackets, windows or swimming alone can have non-weather purposes; do not use native weather intent to settle that ambiguity.
Do not require a positive forecast or committed action: asking whether it will rain expresses rain even if the answer may be no. The task detects the expressed property, not actual weather.

activation_boundary: Only input-expressed typed role; not task-required or generally associated missing parameters.
negative_rule: Full-input reviewed absence under the current policy; native omission never establishes a negative.
ambiguity_rule: Unavailable when property domain or temporal-versus-spatial reading cannot be established from the input.

upstream_evidence.interpretation: Upstream requested time uses query_detail while supplied values use time; weather examples name conditions. This is an explicit new semantic-task choice, not native-annotation equivalence.

evidence.query_regex: \b(how often|how frequently|how long|what time|which time|what is the time|what s the time|whats the time|what is the frequency|what frequency|departure|depart|fare|price|temperature)\b
evidence.reading: All native-positive union and regex-selected contrast reference texts read; not population adjudication or independent review.

scope: Task-wide definitions, no generated reasoning, gold-dependent routing, answer-value recovery or automatic keyword labels.
